title: Tiered Expunge Orchestrator — cross-zone sweep, proof bundles, and customer verification portal
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Customers require a reliable, auditable, and region-aware right-to-be-forgotten flow that can be triggered by users or tenants and produces tamper-evident proof of deletion. Existing purge flows are ad-hoc per-storage backend and lack a unified evidence format and a customer-facing verification path.

Goal: Build a Tiered Expunge Orchestrator that executes staged sweeps (hot cache -> warm storage -> cold archive) across zones/regions, produces signed proof bundles for each tenant sweep, exposes a customer verification portal and an API to download proof bundles, and provides canary/rollback controls for safety. The orchestrator should integrate with KV-cache invalidation, autoscaler hooks (ENG-8842), and evidence-exporter (ENG-9410).
acceptance_criteria: Administrators can initiate tenant-scoped expunge with a single API call and a UI flow in Console
Orchestrator performs ordered stage sweeps: cache invalidation, immediate datastore deletions, background archival expunge, and final tombstone verification
Each sweep generates a signed proof bundle (SHA-256 manifest + signed timestamp) that is stored in the tenant audit store and downloadable via the customer verification portal
Proof bundles include: list of object identifiers removed, region stamp, orchestration run id, and verification checksums for each storage backend
Canary rollout supports targeting 1% of tenants with automatic abort if verification failures > 0.5% in the canary window
Rollback path preserves evidence that a rollback occurred and reasons; deleted artifacts are unrecoverable unless under legal hold exception documented in the bundle
Automated CI checks for performance regressions: expunge throughput (objects/sec) and 99th pct latency for sweep steps
Security review completed and KMS signing keys used for evidence bundle signatures
updates: 2026-02-20 - Grooming: scoped MVP to tenant-scoped expunge + evidence bundle. Decided to defer legal-hold UI to follow-up PM ticket.
2026-02-25 - Eng sync: agreed on staged sweep ordering. ENG-8842 (autoscaler hooks) and ENG-9410 (evidence exporter) listed as dependencies
2026-03-03 - Design review: Console mockups reviewed; design requests explicit tenant consent flows and audit log linkouts (see design doc)
2026-03-05 - Security review kickoff: draft threat model submitted to security (SEC-2026-77). KMS key policy constraints noted as blocker for on-prem deployments
2026-03-08 - Prototype: small end-to-end prototype run on dev cluster. Proof bundle schema drafted and pushed to spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/TIERED-EXPUNGE-SPEC
2026-03-10 - PR opened for orchestrator controller: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4221 (feedback: add idempotency and stronger retry semantics)
2026-03-12 - UX feedback: PM + Design approved initial portal wireframes; Security requested signed timestamps be BSI-compliant (follow-up with SEC)
Next: implement signer integration (ENG-9410), add canary flags, and add e2e tests for proof bundle verification
risks: Cross-region latency can extend expunge windows and increase cost — mitigated by parallelizing non-dependent steps
Incomplete backend connectors: legacy archives may not support signed deletion receipts — plan fallback: include 'unverifiable' marker and operator follow-up
KMS availability for signing proof bundles in private deployments; on-prem customers may require alternate HSM integration
Customer confusion if proof bundles are large or use cryptic identifiers — design portal must translate object ids to friendly descriptors where available
tradeoffs: MVP focuses on tenant-scoped expunge, not per-object UI — reduces scope and delivery time
Choosing deterministic SHA-256 manifests increases proof bundle size slightly but simplifies cross-backend verification
Eager delete vs. soft-delete: MVP will perform hard deletes for standard data, soft-delete for items under retention/legal-hold to balance safety vs. irrecoverability
implementation_notes: Orchestrator will be implemented as a controller service behind a job queue with per-tenant execution context
Proof bundle format: newline-delimited JSON manifest + compressed tarball of signed metadata + PGP signature from platform signing key
Integrate with autoscaler hooks (ENG-8842) to pause scaling during large sweeps to avoid cost spikes
Expose REST endpoints: POST /v1/tenants/{id}/expunge and GET /v1/tenants/{id}/expunge/{run_id}/bundle
Ensure idempotency: repeat runs with same run_id should be no-op after completion; partial failures must produce partial proof bundles with error sections
qa_plan: Unit tests for controller state transitions and idempotency
Integration tests with mock storage backends to assert objects removed and manifest checksums match
End-to-end test that performs a tenant expunge in staging, validates proof bundle signature, and downloads via portal
Canary test harness that simulates 1% tenant population with randomized object sets and verifies <0.5% verification failures
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable for 1% tenants in non-critical regions for 2 weeks; monitor verification rate and errors
Phase 2: expand to 25% with feature gating and outbound customer notification templates
Phase 3: global rollout with default off for legacy tenants; provide migration guide
Rollback: immediate halt of orchestrator and sequence of compensating ops documented; proof bundles mark aborted runs
metrics: time_to_complete_tenant_expunge: p50 <= 10m for small tenants (<=10k objects)
